description: Declarative catalogue of structural ONNX graph patterns that carry deployment risk when a reference export is taken toward a static-shape NPU compiler. Each rule names a detector implemented in slm_lab.graph.inspection and carries a reviewed rationale and mitigation. Severities are review judgements about structural risk, not measured compiler outcomes.
target_context: Primary target: Qualcomm QNN / Hexagon HTP ahead-of-time compilation of the T20 static Qwen3-0.6B reference graphs (see docs/project/plan.md 3.2 and 6.6). Secondary target: ONNX Runtime CPU and CUDA execution providers, where the same patterns usually run but cost partitioning, fallback, or memory traffic rather than a hard failure. No severity here is derived from an executed compile job; T22 is the task that will produce that evidence.

rules.title: Public graph input or output has a non-static dimension
rules.rationale: An ahead-of-time compiler for a fixed-function NPU allocates tensors, tiles loops, and assigns DMA descriptors from concrete dimensions. A symbolic or unset dimension on the public boundary leaves it nothing to allocate against, so the usual outcomes are a converter rejection or a forced host fallback. The T12/T20 contract deliberately exports every boundary tensor with fully static shapes (docs/project/plan.md 6.4 and 6.5), so any non-static boundary dimension is a regression against the contract this project already froze, independent of any particular compiler version.
rules.mitigation: Re-export with dynamic_axes=None and concrete example inputs, or freeze the offending dimension per variant so that each prompt length gets its own static graph. If a dimension must vary, prefer a small bucketed family of static graphs over one dynamic graph.

rules.title: Internal value_info entry has a non-static dimension
rules.rationale: A static public boundary does not guarantee a static interior. When shape inference cannot resolve an intermediate tensor to concrete dimensions, a static-shape backend typically cannot claim the subgraph containing it and partitions around it. On ONNX Runtime the same tensor usually still executes, but the partition boundary costs a copy and blocks fusion. Note that a missing or symbolic value_info entry can also simply mean shape inference was never run or could not propagate through one operator, so this is a signal to investigate rather than proof that the tensor is genuinely dynamic.
rules.mitigation: Run ONNX shape inference and re-check; if a dimension is still symbolic, find the producing node and replace the computed shape with a constant, or constant-fold the shape subgraph.
references: ONNX shape inference over the opset 18 operator set

rules.title: Data-dependent control flow operator present
rules.rationale: If, Loop, and Scan make the executed operator sequence and the number of iterations depend on runtime values. An ahead-of-time accelerator compiler emits one fixed command stream, so it generally cannot express branch selection or a trip count it does not know at compile time; the common outcomes are rejection or execution of the whole region on the host CPU. Whether a specific QNN converter release accepts any of these operators has not been measured in this repository, so this severity describes the structural mismatch rather than an observed compile result.
rules.mitigation: Trace the graph with concrete example inputs so the branch is resolved at export time, or hoist the loop into the host-side generation loop and export only the loop body as a static graph. That is exactly the shape the T12 prefill/decode split already has.

rules.title: Node carries a nested subgraph attribute
rules.rationale: A GRAPH-typed attribute means the model contains a nested graph body with its own scope and its own value_info. Even where the parent operator is supported, nested bodies complicate quantization encoding propagation, memory planning, and partitioning, because the nested tensors are not visible in the top-level graph the compiler plans against. This rule fires independently of the operator identity so that a subgraph carried by an operator not listed in R-CONTROL-FLOW-OP is still surfaced.
rules.mitigation: Flatten or unroll the nested body during export, or split the model so the nested region becomes a separate top-level graph invoked by the host.
references: ONNX opset 18 operator set, GRAPH attribute type

rules.title: Shape-defining operator input is computed rather than constant
rules.rationale: Reshape, Slice, Expand, and Tile take their target shape or bounds as a tensor input. When that input is an initializer or a Constant node the resulting shape is fixed and a static compiler can plan around it. When it is produced by another node, the output shape is only known once the graph runs, which is the classic Shape to Gather to Reshape pattern left behind by tracing frameworks. This is the most common reason an otherwise static export still refuses to compile to a fixed command stream. The detector reports where the pattern occurs; it does not prove the value actually varies, because a computed input can still be constant in practice and removable by constant folding.
rules.mitigation: Run constant folding, or rewrite the export wrapper so shapes come from Python integers rather than from tensor arithmetic on Shape outputs. Re-inspect afterwards to confirm the chain collapsed.

rules.title: Operator whose output shape depends on tensor values
rules.rationale: These operators produce a result whose element count is a function of the data, not of the input shape. No amount of shape inference can bound their output at compile time, so a static allocator has nothing to reserve. On ONNX Runtime they execute but force everything downstream of them into a dynamically shaped region.
rules.mitigation: Replace the selection with a fixed-size masked computation, for example a Where over a full-width tensor plus an explicit valid-length scalar, which is the convention the T12 decode contract already uses.

rules.title: Shape-arithmetic operator present in the graph
rules.rationale: Shape, Size, Range, and ConstantOfShape compute metadata rather than activations. Their presence is normal in a traced export and is not itself a fault, but they are the raw material of the data-dependent shape chains flagged by R-DATA-DEPENDENT-SHAPE-INPUT, and they add small host-side operators that a compiler must either fold away or partition around. This rule is deliberately low severity: it exists to give the reader the population count that the higher-severity shape rules should be read against.
rules.mitigation: None required on its own. If the count is large, run constant folding and compare the count before and after to see how much of it is residue rather than real computation.

rules.title: Indexed scatter or gather operator present
rules.rationale: The fixed-capacity KV-cache write in the decode graph is expressed as an indexed scatter at the current valid_length, so these operators are load-bearing rather than incidental: if the backend cannot lower them, the decode graph loses its whole reason to exist. They are also awkward for accelerators because the write address is a runtime value, which defeats static DMA descriptor generation and, in a quantized pipeline, requires the scattered update and the destination buffer to share one encoding. This repository has not yet run a QNN conversion of these nodes, so the severity reflects how central and how structurally awkward they are, not a measured failure.
rules.mitigation: Consider alternatives evaluated in plan 6.5: a shift buffer, a bucketed or growing cache, a mask-and-blend write using Where against a position-comparison mask, or runtime-managed state if the target runtime exposes it. Any replacement must be validated numerically against the reference before it is adopted.

rules.title: Node uses a non-default operator domain
rules.rationale: A node outside the default ONNX domain is a custom operator whose semantics live in a specific runtime's extension library. Such a node cannot be interpreted by a converter that only implements the standard operator set, and it makes the artifact non-portable across the three target platforms this project must compare. The T20 export is expected to be pure standard ONNX, so any hit here is unexpected and should be investigated before the graph is carried forward.
rules.mitigation: Decompose the custom operator into standard operators, or move it out of the graph and into host code. If it must stay, record which runtimes can execute it and treat the artifact as target-specific rather than as the shared reference.

rules.title: Structured mask, prefix-scan, or contraction operator present
rules.rationale: Trilu builds causal masks, CumSum builds running positions, Einsum expresses a contraction that has not been reduced to MatMul, and TopK is a sort-like reduction. All four are comparatively rare outside transformer exports and are therefore among the first operators to be missing, partially supported, or supported only on a subset of ranks and axes in a given accelerator backend. Support varies by backend and version and has not been measured here, so this is a medium-severity watch item that tells the reader where to look first if a conversion fails.
rules.mitigation: Precompute the causal mask as a constant of the fixed variant shape instead of building it with Trilu or CumSum; rewrite Einsum as explicit Transpose plus MatMul; move TopK sampling out of the graph and into the host generation loop.

rules.title: Cast crosses the float16 and float32 boundary
rules.rationale: The T12 contract stores the KV cache in float16 but returns logits in float32, so casts between the two widths are expected by design and are not a defect. They matter because each one is a real precision boundary: a float32 to float16 cast is where overflow and underflow enter, and a float16 to float32 cast is where a later quantizer must decide which side of the boundary it owns. Counting them by direction tells the reader how many such boundaries a numerical comparison has to account for, and whether any appear in places the contract did not intend.
rules.mitigation: Keep the number of crossings small and deliberate. Confirm each one against the contract, and record per-tensor error at the crossings during the T21 numerical comparison rather than only at the graph output. Casts whose source dtype could not be resolved from the graph are counted separately and should be confirmed by hand.

rules.title: Numerically sensitive elementwise or reduction operator present
rules.rationale: Softmax, Erf, Exp, and Log are transcendental and are usually implemented on fixed-point accelerators by piecewise approximation or lookup, so they are the operators where a quantized graph diverges from the float reference first. ReduceMean, Pow, Sqrt, and Reciprocal are the decomposition of RMSNorm; the reduction accumulates across the hidden dimension and the reciprocal square root has a large dynamic range, which makes this the other classic place low-precision error is introduced. The severity is a precision-review flag, not a claim that any specific backend implements these poorly.
rules.mitigation: Keep normalization and softmax in higher precision when the backend allows a mixed-precision partition, and treat these nodes as the first candidates for per-tensor error inspection in the numerical validation report.

rules.title: Graph boundary carries an unusually large number of tensors
rules.rationale: The decode graph takes the entire fixed-capacity KV cache in as explicit per-layer tensors and returns the entire updated cache out again, so the full cache is copied across the graph boundary on every single generated token even though one token writes only one position per layer. That is the dominant memory-traffic term in the decode step and it grows linearly with cache capacity, which plan 6.5 estimates at roughly 112 MiB at context 1024 and 448 MiB at 4096 in float16. Separate input and output buffers also roughly double live memory. The detector reports the observed boundary tensor counts and, where every shape is static, the exact byte total crossing the boundary per invocation.
rules.mitigation: Prefer runtime-managed or in-place cache state if the target runtime exposes it, or stack per-layer tensors into fewer larger buffers to cut descriptor count. Measure before and after; plan 6.6 is explicit that a reduced tensor or node count is not by itself evidence of an optimization.

rules.title: Large constant tensor stored inline in the graph protobuf
rules.rationale: The T20 export pushes every tensor above 1024 bytes into external data, so a large tensor still living inside the protobuf is one the exporter materialized during tracing rather than a model weight. In the committed reports this rule identifies exactly one such tensor per prefill graph, the float16 Constant attribute at /model/model/Constant_4 with shape [1, 1, S, S]: 0.5 MB at S512, 2 MB at S1024, and 33.5 MB at S4096, which accounts for essentially all of the growth in prefill protobuf size across variants while the external weight file stays byte-identical. That is a fully materialized quadratic attention mask baked into the graph. It costs constant memory and load time on every target, it must be re-materialized rather than derived if the graph is ever re-shaped, and in a quantized pipeline it becomes one more tensor needing an encoding.
rules.mitigation: Rebuild the mask from a small constant plus broadcasting, supply it as a graph input, or at minimum move it to external data. Confirm the protobuf size drops and the numerical result is unchanged. Note that the same tensor is absent from the decode graphs, which attend over the full fixed capacity with a boundary attention_mask instead.

rules.title: Graph node count is large
rules.rationale: An unfolded 28-layer transformer exported with constant folding disabled and eager attention produces a long flat node list. Node count drives converter and compiler wall-clock time, the size of the partitioning search, and how many small operators can end up stranded on the host between accelerator partitions. The threshold is a review convention chosen so that the T20 reference graphs are compared against a fixed line across variants, not a supported limit published by any toolchain.
rules.mitigation: Treat this as a budget to track across the reference, QNN-candidate, and quantized stages. Constant folding and operator fusion should reduce it; record the count at each stage so that a change in compile behaviour can be attributed.
